# observe_reference_table

A reference table represents a source of non-temporal data being ingested into Observe.
## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "observe_reference_table" "example" {
  label       = "Example"
  source_file = "path/to/reference_table.csv"
  checksum    = filemd5("path/to/reference_table.csv") // must always be filemd5(source_file)
  description = "State Populations"
  primary_key = ["state_code"]
  label_field = "state_name"

  schema {
    name = "state_code"
    type = "string"
  }

  schema {
    name = "state_name"
    type = "string"
  }

  schema {
    name = "population"
    type = "int64"
  }
}
```
<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) The name of the reference table name. Must be unique within workspace.

### Optional

- `checksum` (String) MD5 checksum of the source file.
Can be computed using `filemd5("<source_file>")`. Required with `source_file`, and must not be set with `initial_source_file`.
- `description` (String) Description for the reference table.
- `initial_source_file` (String) The path to a CSV file whose rows seed the reference table when it is created. After that, Terraform does not manage the rows: rows edited in Observe, in the UI or through the API, are kept, and changes to this file are ignored. `label`, `description` and `primary_key` can still be updated. Changing `schema` or `label_field` fails the plan, because the API applies either only with an upload, which would replace the rows edited in Observe. To change them, switch to `source_file` in the same apply: the file replaces every row and the table keeps its dataset, and you can switch back to `initial_source_file` afterwards. Switching to `source_file` uploads that file on the next apply if its checksum differs from the table's. Exactly one of `source_file` and `initial_source_file` must be set.
- `label_field` (String) The field that should be used for the OPAL label.
- `primary_key` (List of String) The primary key of the reference table.
- `schema` (Block List) The schema of the reference table. Must match the columns in the source file. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--schema))
- `source_file` (String) The path to a CSV file containing the reference table data. Terraform manages the rows: when `checksum` changes, the file is uploaded and replaces every row, including rows edited in Observe. Exactly one of `source_file` and `initial_source_file` must be set.

### Read-Only

- `dataset` (String) The Observe ID for the dataset managed by the reference table.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `oid` (String) OID (Observe ID) for this object. This is the canonical identifier that
should be used when referring to this object in terraform manifests.

<a id="nestedblock--schema"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schema`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name of the column.
- `type` (String) The type of the column. See https://docs.observeinc.com/en/latest/content/query-language-reference/OPALUserGuideTypesOperators.html for options.
